statement: The node answers a dispute its peer started against it in the epoch it is in. The Entity keeps the dispute (`against`: the nonce and author the dispute opened with, the hash of its body, the end of its window and whether the chain's clock has passed it; the first one told for the epoch is kept, one of another epoch is not this record's). While it is open the node asks for ONE counter with the newest proof it holds, when the chain would rank that proof above the one the dispute opened with (a higher nonce, or the same nonce authored by Left against Right's): the head must be the one the peer signed, the nonce is the epoch's first plus the slot, less one, the body is the one its committed state signs as, and the signature is the peer's own over that head, kept in `proofs` (R-SIGNED-HEADS-ON-THE-WIRE). The counter names the dispute it answers (its nonce and body hash) and is restated at every frame until the chain registers it (`j_countered`, which both parties hear), so that it lands inside the floor window (60 + 60 s on testnet); a Host that restarts is asked again. A dispute that opened with the newest proof the node holds, one the node started, and one of another epoch are not countered; with no co-signed proof of the epoch there is nothing to counter with. Once the window is over and the chain registered the node's counter, the node asks to finalize (`dispute_finalize`) with the counter's nonce, author, body and the side that started the dispute, naming the dispute it answers, and keeps asking until `j_dispute_over`: after a registered counter the chain finalizes only the counter's proof, and by either party. The Host reads the window of an answered dispute as it reads that of a started one. The starter that hears the counter stops asking to finalize with its opening proof, which the chain would revert; once the window is over it finalizes with the registered counter itself (the chain lets either party execute it) when one of the states it holds, the committed one or the one a frame of its own in flight would commit, has the body hash the chain logged for the counter, and asks again at each frame until `j_dispute_over`. A body it cannot rebuild is not guessed, since the chain would revert a finalize that names another (owed: the body from the counter's calldata). The node a dispute was started against, whose newest proof is the opening state and that has no counter to ask for, finalizes that state at once, without waiting for the window, when one of its states has the body hash the chain logged for the start: the chain lets the non-starter accept the exact state the starter chose (Account.sol 861-875), so a starter that goes down leaves the Account no more locked than one that stays up. A body it cannot rebuild is waited out as before (owed: the body from the start's calldata), and a finalize the chain would revert before the window (a proof body with a Pull) is dropped by the Host and asked again at each frame. A node with a dispute open against it asks for none of its own (`dispute_pending`): the chain would skip the start (DISPUTE_ACTIVE) with no event, and the Host waits on the window of the dispute against the node whenever its own start has none (`windowsOf`). A counter the chain will refuse for good lapses like a start (R-DISPUTE-LAPSED) and is not restated; one that can heal is. Not here: a frame sealed before the dispute was heard and committed after the node's counter (R-DISPUTE-FREEZE stops every other), a counter whose proof holds an open clause (S9 exercises the clause side), a secret shown only in a dispute's arguments (R-WATCH-CALLDATA reads it), and both sides disputing at once.
